problem: Person-following robots lose the target under occlusion; vision-only trackers suffer ID switches, and kinematic (constant-velocity) coasting gives implausible predictions (through walls, missed turns), causing freezing or mission failure.
motivation: Indoor human-centric environments are structured (corridors, intersections, left-hand walking convention), so occluded target motion is constrained by the map. Exploiting this prior can guide the robot to reacquire the target instead of coasting blindly.
key_idea: When the vision+LiDAR EKF track is lost, run BFS on a predefined topological map of walking lanes to propagate the target's last known state into a discrete set of feasible future paths and feed them to a DWA local planner for reacquisition.
insight: Map-structured multi-hypothesis prediction (continue straight vs. turn, with turning branches prioritized when straight is in line of sight) provides plausible guidance during occlusions that short-horizon kinematic EKF coasting cannot. However, the paper has no ablation against a pure-EKF baseline, so the benefit is supported only by a 71.4% reacquisition rate on 7 occlusion events (5 ID-switches, 2 re-tag failures).
method: Detection and tracking: YOLOv8n person detection on RealSense RGB, DeepSORT for consistent IDs of the tagged person.
Camera-to-LiDAR fusion: a calibrated homography projects the bounding box to the ground plane as a seed; VLP-16 scan (downsampled to 2D) is clustered within a 0.5 m radius to get the target center.

Target EKF: 4-state (x,y,θ,v) unicycle model, Q=diag(0.05,0.05,0.1,0.1), R=diag(0.1,0.1), observing only x,y; coasts on occlusion, resets to camera projection if drift >1.0 m, prunes the track after 5 s without updates.
Localization: EKF fusing wheel odometry and IMU, plus AMCL, with LiDAR SLAM map.

Map-informed recovery: BFS over a topological graph (nodes = intersections/corners, directed edges = left-side lanes) up to a max path length from last known position and velocity, yielding discrete future trajectories; straight branches within line of sight are deprioritized.
Local planning: DWA consumes the predicted paths to move the robot toward likely target positions until visual reacquisition.

setting.backbone: YOLOv8n + DeepSORT (pretrained, used as-is) with EKF, BFS on topological map, DWA
setting.training_data: none (no training in this work; pretrained detector/tracker used)
setting.observation: RealSense RGB-D camera (RGB used), Velodyne VLP-16 LiDAR downsampled to 2D scan, IMU, wheel odometry
setting.action_space: continuous velocity commands (v ≤ 0.4 m/s, ω ≤ 1.5 rad/s) from DWA on a differential-drive robot
setting.privileged: predefined topological map of walking lanes with left-hand convention

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; only real-world results (71.4% reacquisition success over 7 major occlusion events, 5 trials, 20 minutes total) are given in text, without a benchmark table.
results: On a real robot in 5 trials with 1–11 people, the map-informed recovery reacquired the target in 71.4% of 7 major occlusions (1–7 s blockage, reacquire up to 10 s), with 5 ID-switches and 2 re-tag failures. YOLOv8n ran at 16.2 FPS. No baseline comparison is reported.
limitations: Very small evaluation (7 occlusion events, 5 trials) with no baseline or ablation such as pure-EKF coasting
Requires a predefined topological map and assumes a left-walking convention, limiting use in unstructured or crowd-flow settings
ID-switches and re-tag failures remain in dense scenes
builds_on: MIPP (map-informed path prediction, authors' prior work)
version: deepread-v1 (2026-09-29): full text + insight + evidence-checked numbers
